data.title: Dowling–Degos disease — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Dowling–Degos disease** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What is Dowling–Degos disease (DDD)?**
- Rare autosomal dominant reticulate pigmentary disorder of flexures ('reticulate pigmented anomaly of the flexures'), onset in adolescence/adulthood, slowly progressive
- Genes: KRT5 (loss of function), POFUT1, POGLUT1, PSENEN (latter also with hidradenitis suppurativa)

**Q2. Clinical features.**
- Small brown-black macules coalescing into reticulate (net-like) pigmentation in axillae, groin, neck, inframammary, antecubital, inner thighs; may extend to trunk and face
- Comedo-like dark follicular papules on back/neck, pitted perioral acneiform scars, epidermoid cysts, hidradenitis suppurativa (PSENEN), mild itch

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Filiform/antler-like elongation of thin, pigmented rete ridges ('finger-like' downgrowths) with basal hyperpigmentation, including follicular infundibula; horn cysts; no increase in melanocytes
- Galli–Galli disease: same + suprabasal acantholysis

**Q4. Enumerate reticulate pigmentary disorders.**
- Dowling–Degos disease (flexural), reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura (dorsa of hands/feet with palmar pits), Galli–Galli disease (DDD + acantholysis), dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria (Dohi — acral hypo+hyperpigmented macules, ADAR1), dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria, Naegeli–Franceschetti–Jadassohn and dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis (keratin 14, absent dermatoglyphics), dyskeratosis congenita (reticulate pigmentation, nail dystrophy, leukoplakia), X-linked reticulate pigmentary disorder, incontinentia pigmenti stage 3, confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, prurigo pigmentosa, macular amyloidosis, erythema ab igne, poikiloderma

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Acanthosis nigricans (velvety, not reticulate), reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura (acral), Haber's syndrome (rosacea-like face + DDD-like), frictional pigmentation, confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, Galli–Galli, erythrasma, LPP inverse

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Difficult; reassurance; topical retinoids, hydroquinone, azelaic acid (modest); Er:YAG/CO2/Q-switched lasers (variable); oral retinoids for comedonal component; treat associated hidradenitis

## Quick spotter facts
- Reticulate flexural pigmentation + comedo-like papules + perioral pits — Dowling–Degos
- Antler-like pigmented rete ridges

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Reticulate pigmentary disorders). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
